headline: Ranger Suarez Flirts With History As Sox Finally Break Slump In Seattle
morning_brew: Ranger Suarez was absolutely electric out in Seattle last night. He carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning, completely baffling the Mariners and leading us to a much-needed six to two win. He finished with six and two-thirds innings of scoreless baseball, giving up just one hit and striking out five. After that brutal sweep in Toronto, seeing Ranger dominate like that was exactly what the doctor ordered.

The bats actually showed up too, racking up ten hits. We broke it open with four runs in the seventh, which gave our bullpen a nice cushion. Tommy Kahnle made things a little interesting by giving up two runs in the ninth, but we held on to secure the victory. My neighbor Rick was so excited he nearly woke up the entire block when Suarez was chasing that no-no in the sixth. It is only one win, but when you're sitting at thirty and forty-three, you take every single positive you can get.

Down in Foxborough, things are quiet after spring practices wrapped up, but the front office needs to keep an eye on the remaining free agents to help out Drake Maye. As for our Sox, they've got game two against the Mariners tonight, and we need another strong performance to build some real momentum before heading to Colorado.
